newsitem.title: USA: Russia Vnesh loans remain lower in late U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: Russia Vnesh loans remain lower in late U.S. trade.

text.p: Russian Vneshekonombank loans rebounded from early morning lows but prices still remained weaker in late afternoon on news that President Boris Yeltsin fired security chief Alexander Lebed, market sources said.

"It's been a crazy day. It's been very choppy but overall positive on the back of the (U.S. long Treasury) bond being much stronger," said one emerging markets trader, who noted that the paring of losses of Russian paper helped the market.
Vnesh dollar loans were off 7/8 at 76 after falling as much as 2-1/2 earlier, and Russian Swiss franc laons were down 1-1/8 at 73-1/8 bid.
Vnesh mark loans were 7/8 softer at 80-1/8.
Following the action taken by Yeltsin, both Standard and Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service Inc said the removal of Lebed would not affect their current rating decisions.
S&P rates Russia's foreign currency debt at BB-minus and Moody's rates the country's sovereign ceiling on its foreign currency debt a prospective Ba2.
Sources said strength in the U.S. Treasury market, a stronger peso and the bouncing back of Vnesh paper to opening levels all helped to bolster the broader market.
Brazilian C bonds rose 1/2 to 71-3/4, while Mexico's global bond due 2026 firmed 3/8 to 99-3/4 and Argentine pars firmed 3/4 to 58-1/8.
Elsewhere, Ecuador's par bonds were one percentage point higher at 42-1/2 and Morocco Series A bonds were 1/4 firmer at 78-5/8.
